keyVerseText: Thou hast enlarged my steps under me; so that my feet did not slip. feet: Heb. ankles
rootMeaning: The root of קַרְסֹל (qarçôl) is קָרַס (qâraç), which means 'to stoop' or 'to bend down.' This etymology suggests that the noun form refers to a part of the body associated with bending or joint movement, specifically the ankle. Unlike the simple English word 'foot,' the root highlights the ankle's function as a joint that enables stooping or bending, emphasizing mobility and flexibility rather than just a static body part.
usageInScripture: The word קַרְסֹל appears only twice in Scripture, consistently translated with reference to the ankle or foot area. Both top translations relate to the phrase 'under me so that my feet' or 'under me that my feet,' indicating a focus on stability and movement. This consistency in usage underscores the term's specific anatomical reference to the ankle, the joint that supports and steadies the foot during walking or standing.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding קַרְסֹל as the ankle—the joint that supports movement—adds depth to biblical imagery of walking and standing firm in faith. It reminds believers that their spiritual journey involves not just a static position but dynamic movement empowered by God. The ankle's role in balance and flexibility metaphorically reflects the believer's dependence on divine strength to remain steadfast and to progress in holiness. This word thus enriches our appreciation of God's sustaining power in the believer's daily walk.
keyVerseReflection: In 2 Samuel 22:37, the psalmist declares, 'Thou hast enlarged my steps under me; so that my feet did not slip,' with 'feet' referring specifically to the ankles. The use of קַרְסֹל here highlights God's enabling power to stabilize the believer's movement and prevent slipping. It conveys a vivid picture of divine support that secures the very joints that bear weight and allow progress, affirming God's role as the foundation of our spiritual stability.
